verdicts.note: A real limitation of BM25 that motivates hybrid search; the strength claim stays true without it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Embeddings are weaker on exact codes and identifiers.
verdicts.claimQuote: Passages that mean the same thing end up close together even when they share no words
verdicts.note: Limitation of vector retrieval (31 of 50 code queries missed); the semantic-matching claim remains true but the weakness must be in the notes.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Embeddings must also be recomputed whenever the encoder changes, which for this collection takes about 6 hours.
verdicts.claimQuote: Vector retrieval turns the query and every passage into embeddings
verdicts.note: An operational cost of vector retrieval, not a falsifier of any claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: when lexical and semantic signals are complementary, that is, when each retriever finds relevant passages that the other misses
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence condition, reinforced by u18's failure cases; 'hybrid improves recall' stated unconditionally is misleading.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Each retriever returns its top 50 passages, so the fused list holds at most 100 candidates
verdicts.note: A configuration parameter and its arithmetic consequence; it does not limit another claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: the cross-encoder runs only on the fused candidates, never on the whole collection
verdicts.claimQuote: it judges relevance far more accurately than either retriever
verdicts.note: Cost-driven scope restriction on the reranker; the accuracy claim stays true, but the scope matters (it underpins u32).

verdicts.conditionQuote: but it does not guarantee that the final answer is correct. The reranker can only reorder what retrieval found: if the right passage is not among the candidates, reranking cannot recover it.
verdicts.claimQuote: Reranking improves the precision of the top results
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence 'but' plus u32/u33 limits; stating that reranking improves results without them implies it fixes retrieval misses or ensures correct answers. u49 restates the same caveat in the summary.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If none of the passages addresses the question, it should say so rather than answer from its general knowledge.
verdicts.claimQuote: is instructed to answer only from them and to cite the passages it used
verdicts.note: A fallback rule for the no-relevant-passage case; the generation instruction claim stays true without it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: but they do not show whether the passage itself is current
verdicts.claimQuote: Citations let a reader check each claim against its passage
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence caveat; without it citations would read as a guarantee of correctness/currency.

verdicts.conditionQuote: These figures come from one collection and one query set; a collection with fewer exact identifiers may see a smaller gain from BM25, and a different reranker will have a different latency.
verdicts.note: Generalisation limit on the whole results table (u41-u45); reporting the numbers as general would be misleading.
A data row of the results table, not a limit on any claim.

verdicts.claimQuote: Teams with a strict latency budget can rerank fewer candidates
verdicts.note: Intra-sentence trade-off; without it reranking fewer candidates reads as a free latency saving. Could alternatively be read as a set-level option limiting u45's latency cost.

additional.conditionQuote: Raising the limit to 100 per retriever put the right passage in the list slightly more often, but it roughly doubled the time spent reranking, so we kept 50.
additional.claimQuote: Each retriever returns its top 50 passages

additional.conditionQuote: Reranking adds about 120 ms per query, most of it spent running the cross-encoder over up to 100 candidates, and it accounts for most of the cost increase.
additional.note: Latency and cost price of the reranker's relevance gain; the gain stays true but the cost must be kept.
